headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: AutoGen can write broad outputs into gpt-researcher’s API-backed research pipeline, with shared file and network surfaces amplifying misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can write files and emit stdout/stderr, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and supports MCP/API-driven ingestion. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if AutoGen output is fed into gpt-researcher without filtering. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF AutoGen output is copied into gpt-researcher prompts or source documents
IF gpt-researcher treats retrieved file content as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents with distinct workspaces
Strip instruction-like text before passing outputs onward
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores embedded directives
Review one sample handoff for prompt-injection markers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content, and AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys while gpt-researcher handles multiple external APIs and local documents. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow into both systems and then out through gpt-researcher’s API calls. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory
IF sensitive documents are present in that directory
IF gpt-researcher sends retrieved content to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Remove secrets from shared folders
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Run a quick file-permission audit

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; gpt-researcher can also read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. Even without explicit git overlap, concurrent writes and package changes in a shared environment can collide and corrupt work products. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same writable directory
IF package installation or subprocess side effects target shared state
mitigations: Assign each agent its own workspace
Pin dependencies before running both
Avoid concurrent execution in the same directory
Check for lockfile or temp-file collisions

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can generate intermediate outputs, and gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can turn retrieved content into reports. That makes A’s output a likely input to B’s downstream actions with limited verification, so a mistaken or manipulated AutoGen result can cascade into published research. The default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher consumes AutoGen-produced drafts or facts
IF the publisher step runs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before publishing
Add a verification step against primary sources
Pass only structured data, not free-form claims
Log provenance for each imported fact

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and broad filesystem content, while gpt-researcher processes local documents, citations, and images through external APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into the shared workflow, the pair can create retention and jurisdiction mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in research inputs
IF external APIs retain prompts or documents beyond policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workflow
Use region-locked API endpoints
Review retention settings before each run
Keep an audit note of data classes processed
